items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was writing for Louis Jordan. ... I did write one for Louis Jordan called I’ll Die Happy ... I wrote that for Louis Jordan. He recorded that on Decca.

ctx.x: I guess this is – what? – in the ’52 to ’54 time period? You had written Four Brothers. I guess you were doing a lot of writing during that period.

I was writing for Louis Jordan. I was writing what I call unpopular songs. But I did write one for Louis Jordan called I’ll Die Happy, which was chosen number one rhythm-and-blues song of 1957 by Cash Box on the cover.
